blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A financial ratio is just one number divided by another. It shows something simple that is hard to see in the raw figures. Ratios turn big piles of numbers into small, comparable stories.

Profit margin is profit divided by revenue. It tells you how much of every pound ends up as profit. Current ratio is current assets divided by current liabilities. It tells you if the company can pay its short-term bills. Inventory turnover tells you how many times a year the stock is sold and replaced.

Ratios are how accountants and managers talk about a business without drowning in detail. But one good ratio is not enough. A number only means something when you compare it with another period or another team.

items.q: What is a financial ratio?
options: A long list of raw figures
The total profit of the year
items.why: "A financial ratio is just one number divided by another."

items.q: What does profit margin tell you?
options: How many bills the company must pay
How much of every pound ends up as profit
How many times the stock is sold
How many people work in finance
items.why: "It tells you how much of every pound ends up as profit."

items.q: The current ratio tells you if the company can…
items.why: "It tells you if the company can pay its short-term bills."

items.q: The text suggests that the author would most likely DISAGREE with…
options: "One ratio alone gives you the full picture."
"Managers use ratios to talk about a business."
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que um número só significa algo quando é comparado — um ratio sozinho não basta.

items.q: "Ratios turn big piles of numbers into small stories" suggests that ratios are useful because they…
items.why: Inferência: transformar pilhas de números em histórias pequenas = tornar a informação mais simples.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry ajudando a nova analista. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let's look at these three months of accounts together. Don't worry — ratios are simpler than they look. Each one is just one number divided by another.

Start with the profit margin. This month it is twelve per cent. Last month it was ten. So for every hundred pounds we earned, twelve pounds became profit. That is a small rise, and it is good news.

Now the current ratio. It is one point five. That means we have one and a half pounds in current assets for every pound of current liabilities. So yes, we can pay our short-term bills. If that number falls below one, we should worry.

Last, inventory turnover. The stock was sold and replaced eight times this quarter. Higher is usually better, because it means we are not sitting on old stock.

Here is my one rule: never read a ratio alone. Always compare it with another month or another desk. One number on its own can fool you.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the profit margin this month?
items.why: "This month it is twelve per cent. Last month it was ten."

items.q: What does a current ratio of one point five mean?
options: One and a half pounds in current assets for every pound of current liabilities
The stock is sold one and a half times a year
Profit is one and a half per cent
items.why: "one and a half pounds in current assets for every pound of current liabilities."

items.q: How many times was the stock sold and replaced this quarter?
items.why: "the stock was sold and replaced eight times this quarter."

items.q: Harry says that if the current ratio falls below one, the company should worry. Why?
options: Because it may not be able to pay its short-term bills
Because the stock is too new
Because it has too many current assets
items.why: Inferência: abaixo de 1, os ativos circulantes não cobrem os passivos circulantes — risco de não pagar as contas.

items.q: What is Harry's main advice about reading ratios?
options: Always read a ratio on its own
Always compare a ratio with another month or desk
Only look at the profit margin
items.why: Inferência: "never read a ratio alone… Always compare" — comparar é a regra central dele.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A financial ratio compares two numbers." A ratio is…
items.why: Ratio = índice / razão: um número dividido por outro.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The profit margin shows what percentage of ___ becomes profit."
items.why: Profit margin = margem de lucro: lucro dividido pela receita (revenue).

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Cash and stock are examples of a current ___."
items.why: Current asset = ativo circulante, como caixa e estoque.

items.q: "Inventory turnover is high." This means the stock is…
items.why: Inventory turnover = giro de estoque: quantas vezes o estoque é vendido e reposto.

items.q: "Ratios help us talk about a business without drowning in detail." To drown in detail means to…
options: get lost in too much information
items.why: To drown = afogar-se: aqui, ficar perdido em detalhes demais.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre números e resultados. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the monthly report." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Let's go over these three ratios together." To go over means to…
items.why: Go over = revisar, passar por algo com atenção.

items.q: "A single ratio can be misleading, so we should not rely on it alone." To rely on means to…
items.why: Rely on = depender de / confiar em.

items.q: "Higher inventory turnover should move the needle on profit." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "The current ratio is going down." This means it is…
items.why: Going down = caindo, diminuindo.
